architecture.fell_back_and_why: The plugin subagents (ehs-*) are not installed in this environment, so per references/team.md 'Dispatching without the plugin subagents' every role ran as a general-purpose subagent with the role-file path, its pack paths, the safety contract, the mode, the target language and the return format copied into the prompt verbatim, plus the `searched` requirement passed down word for word. No specialist failed to return, so no coverage was dropped and no partial-report fallback was needed. Dispatch was in waves under a hard cap of four concurrent agents: wave 1 (web-api, ai-safety, infra-cloud, mobile), wave 2 (supply-chain, privacy-abuse) launched while web-api was still running to avoid idling at three in flight, wave 3 (two blind verifiers). VER-09 blindness was made structural rather than promised: the verifiers read claim files containing only assertion and path:line, and a grep confirmed no evidence, impact or recommendation prose leaked into them. Two corrections were applied at consolidation: ehs-web-api cited FP-17 and FP-23, neither of which exists (the corpus defines FP-01..FP-11 only), so those two triage entries were dropped while both findings retained their valid rules; and the leader's first inventory was extension-filtered and missed WebPane.tsx and app.env.j2, both of which were caught by the owning specialists and are covered here. findings.title: The /ops/ edge location forwards client-supplied identity headers, so any caller can mint an ops-admin actor
findings.class: Broken authentication / BFLA (CWE-290, CWE-863)
findings.evidence: edge.conf:39-48 (location /v1/) overwrites X-Forwarded-Subject and X-Forwarded-Account and pins X-Forwarded-Roles to "". edge.conf:60-67 (location /ops/) sets only Host, X-Real-IP and X-Forwarded-For, so nginx forwards the client's own identity headers verbatim. requireSession (auth.ts:52) falls back to actorFromHeaders when no bearer token is present, and actorFromHeaders (auth.ts:19-28) builds the Actor entirely from those three headers. adminOps (accounts.ts:107-112) then authorizes on hasRole(actor,'ops-admin'). ssl_verify_client is optional (edge.conf:33), so no client certificate is required.
findings.impact: A request to /ops/ carrying no credential but X-Forwarded-Roles: ops-admin is authenticated and authorized as an operator: unauthenticated read of any account and its member roster (accounts.ts:113-116) and unauthenticated write of any account's plan (accounts.ts:117-122).
findings.recommendation: Set the three X-Forwarded-* identity headers in every location that proxies to the app, including /ops/, /oauth/token and /healthz. Better: blank them once at server level and set them per location, so a newly added location fails closed. Consider requiring ssl_verify_client on for /ops/.

triage.reason: No layer between nginx and the handler re-derives identity; auth.ts:52 is the only construction of Actor and it reads the headers directly.
The omission is as wide as it reads: every route under the /ops prefix mounted at index.ts:25, none narrower.
edge.conf is the shipped edge config and adminOps is mounted unconditionally at index.ts:25 with no flag or environment gate.

scope.established_by: Joined the nginx location list against the Elysia mount list, then traced each identity header to its only reader.
scope.narrowed_by: A request presenting a valid bearer token takes the JWT branch first (auth.ts:52); the spoof works because omitting Authorization is free.

findings.title: Entitlement resolution falls open to the enterprise tier for any unrecognised or missing plan code

findings.title: The idempotency claim is never released on failure, so one failed payout suppresses that key for seven days
findings.class: Business flow abuse / denial of a financial operation (CWE-754, CWE-770)

Every retry then takes the !claim.fresh branch and returns {status:'in-flight'} (payoutRelease.js:15) instead of paying. The key is also chosen by the producer (p.idempotencyKey ?? envelope.id) and namespaced only by the literal prefix 'ik'.

That unvalidated value is then joined into a filesystem path (tools.py:32) followed by a directory creation and a write, and interpolated into the system prompt (assistant.py:110). Neither sink canonicalises the result or checks that it stays under the configured root. The note name itself is pattern-bound, so the tenant is the only free segment.
findings.impact: Bounded today, and the reason matters: the tenant header IS on the gateway strip list, so an outside caller cannot set it. What remains is that no containment check stands between an identity value and a directory creation plus write, and none stands between an identity value and the system prompt - so the safety of both sinks rests entirely on a header-stripping rule in a different system.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same pattern in the principal builder that the ingest model already applies, and share the constant between them so the two definitions cannot drift. Independently, resolve the note directory and assert the result is relative to the configured root before writing.

triage.reason: Scoped to the construct reported - the absence of containment on the path join and of validation on the header - which applies on every note write regardless of who set the header. The spoofing route is separately narrowed and is not claimed.

Downgraded to low precisely because the tenant header is stripped by the gateway, so the value is gateway-supplied. The finding is still written down because the control that bounds it lives in another system and this code asserts nothing.
Unusually, the artifact is present: the strip list in the repository does cover this header, which supports the downgrade rather than an UNKNOWN.

scope.established_by: Compared the two places the same field is constructed, then followed the unvalidated one to each of its sinks.
scope.narrowed_by: beacon.yaml:26 puts the tenant header on the gateway strip list, so the value is not caller-supplied at the boundary - the difference from the groups header, where the equivalent line is missing.

searched.for: whether the tenant header is stripped, which is what separates this from the groups finding
searched.found: it IS listed - this is what downgraded the finding from high to low, and it is the check that stopped a path-traversal claim that could not be stood behind

searched.for: a resolve or relative-to containment assertion after the join
searched.found: nothing - a directory creation and a write on the joined path as given

searched.for: a shared validator or pattern constant reused from the ingest model
searched.found: nothing - the two definitions of the same field are independent, which is the drift this reports

findings.title: All five manifests use floating version ranges and no lockfile exists anywhere in the tree
findings.class: Non-deterministic dependency resolution (CWE-1357, CWE-1104)
findings.evidence: Caret ranges in pulsegate-api/package.json:13-21, tallyflow-consumer/package.json:13-17 and harborlight-mobile/package.json:12-23; unbounded lower-bound floors in beaconindex/pyproject.toml:7-12 and quarrystore/pyproject.toml:7-12. A recursive search for every lockfile format in both ecosystems across the whole corpus returned zero files. The tree is not a git repository, so git-history secret scanning was not available and was not performed - stated rather than implied.
findings.impact: If no lock exists in the real repository, every install re-resolves to whatever satisfies the range at that moment, so two deploys of the same commit can ship different code and a compromised patch release of any direct or transitive dependency is picked up automatically. It also means the exact resolved versions - and any advisory against them - are not determinable from this artifact. Reachability is NOT APPLICABLE: this is a resolution-integrity finding, and no CVE is asserted, because with no lock and no network the installed versions cannot be established.
findings.recommendation: Commit the lockfile for the three applications, all of which are marked private, and install with a frozen-lockfile command in CI; for the Python components pin a resolved, hashed set for the deployed artifact. Then run an offline dependency scan against the resolved tree.

triage.reason: The control that would settle this - a committed lockfile plus the real CI install command - lives outside what was provided. The tree has no git directory, no CI directory and no Dockerfile, so the evidence cannot be obtained, and absence of evidence is never HOLDS. This caps the finding at probable.
The three npm manifests declare private: true, so the library exculpation does not apply to them; they are applications, where a committed lock is expected.
Bounded to low: the ranges alone are ordinary practice, and the impact depends entirely on the lock question that could not be settled. Downgraded, not deleted.

scope.established_by: Read each manifest's dependency block key by key and ran a recursive filename search for every lockfile format in both ecosystems.
scope.narrowed_by: beaconindex and quarrystore are distributable Python packages, where an uncommitted lock is expected by design; the finding is strongest on the three private applications.

searched.for: any lockfile that would make the floating ranges deterministic
searched.found: nothing - zero lockfiles of any format anywhere in the 60-file tree

searched.for: an internal registry or proxy freezing versions, which is the stated exculpation - .npmrc, .yarnrc, pip.conf, index-url, publishConfig, registry overrides
searched.found: nothing - no registry configuration of any kind

searched.for: CI workflows or a Dockerfile carrying the real install command, which would settle whether the lock is used
searched.found: nothing - no CI config and no Dockerfile; this is what forced the FP-08 answer to UNKNOWN

searched.for: install lifecycle hooks (preinstall/postinstall/prepare), overrides/resolutions, scope confusion or typosquat candidates - the other defects a manifest hides
searched.found: none; 30 dependency names all correctly spelled real packages, private: true set on all three, no lifecycle hook anywhere. Recorded as a clean result, not a skipped check.
